questions.question: In a double or triple combination:

options.text: Cargo weight must be evenly distributed between all trailers.
The heaviest trailer should be closest to the cab.
The heaviest trailer should be in the rear.
The weight of the trailers does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: The heaviest trailer should be closest to the cab.
questions.explanation: Place the heaviest trailer closest to the tractor. Place the lightest trailer in the rear.

questions.question: Large combination vehicles take the longest time to stop when:
questions.explanation: Empty vehicles take longer to stop than loaded ones. With less weight, the wheels have less grip on the road.

questions.question: Avoid sudden lane changes by:

options.text: Using your horn to encourage other drivers to move.
Only driving slower than the speed limit.
Looking ahead down the road while driving.
Pulling off the road when traffic is heavy.

questions.correctAnswerText: Looking ahead down the road while driving.
questions.explanation: Look ahead for obstacles that may require a lane change. This helps you avoid sudden lane changes, which are dangerous with combination vehicles.

questions.question: The service air line is attached to the:
questions.explanation: The service air line carries air controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It connects to relay valves, which apply the trailer brakes quickly.

questions.question: If the emergency air line loses pressure, it will cause:

options.text: The tractor protection valve to open.

questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes. When air pressure is lost, the emergency trailer brakes activate.

questions.question: Combination vehicles need more road space than other commercial vehicles because they are longer and:

options.text: Need more space to turn and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need more space to turn and stop.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more road space because they are longer and need more space to turn and stop. Managing space properly is important when driving these vehicles.

questions.question: To reduce the risk of a rollover, you should:

options.text: Load cargo as far forward as possible.
Load cargo as far back as possible.
Load cargo as low as possible.
Stack cargo as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Load cargo as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Load cargo as close to the ground as possible to reduce rollover risk. Also take curves and corners slowly.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Makes turning a large vehicle easier.

questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents the wheels from locking up during hard braking.

questions.question: If you are unsure whether a trailer has ABS, you can:

options.text: Check under the trailer for wheel speed sensors on the brakes.
Drive on a slippery surface to see if ABS activates.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check under the trailer for wheel speed sensors on the brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built after March 1, 1998 must have ABS, shown by a yellow warning light. For older trailers, check under them for wiring from wheel speed sensors on the brakes.

questions.question: An air supply control lever should be in "normal" position when you are:
questions.explanation: In older vehicles, tractor protection controls may use levers. When an air supply control is in "normal" position, you are ready to pull a trailer.

questions.question: If your trailer goes off course while backing, what should you do?

options.text: Continue backing without making any changes.
Move forward, adjust your position, and back up again.
Get out and push the trailer into the correct position.
Turn the steering wheel all the way left until the trailer straightens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward, adjust your position, and back up again.
questions.explanation: If your trailer goes off course while backing, move forward and reposition your vehicle before backing up again.

questions.question: Driving a combination vehicle requires _____ skill than driving a single vehicle.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more skill to drive than single vehicles. They are longer and heavier, making them more likely to roll over.

questions.question: If your trailer begins to skid, you should:
questions.explanation: If your trailer skids while braking, release the brakes. This lets the wheels regain grip on the road. Once traction returns, the trailer will straighten out and follow the truck.

questions.question: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, the trailer height should be:

options.text: Slightly higher than the fifth wheel center.
Level with the fifth wheel center.
Slightly lower than the fifth wheel center.
Next to the fifth wheel center.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slightly lower than the fifth wheel center.
questions.explanation: When connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer, the trailer height should be slightly lower than the fifth wheel center.

questions.question: Fully-loaded rigs:

options.text: Are less likely to roll over than empty rigs.
Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
Are just as likely to roll over as empty rigs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are more likely to roll over than empty rigs.
questions.explanation: Fully-loaded rigs are 10 times more likely to roll over than empty rigs because the cargo creates a higher center of gravity.

questions.question: What is off-tracking?

options.text: When the front wheels follow a different path than the rear wheels.
When all wheels follow the same path.
When the load shifts during a turn.
When wheels go over a curb during a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the front wheels follow a different path than the rear wheels.
questions.explanation: Off-tracking happens when a vehicle turns a corner. The rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels.

questions.question: To prevent a trailer from rolling over, you should:

options.text: Speed up when approaching a corner.
Take on-ramps faster than the posted speed.

questions.explanation: To prevent rollovers, keep cargo low and drive slowly around turns.

questions.question: When coupling glad hands, match the colors. Service lines are often:
questions.explanation: When coupling glad hands, match the colors to avoid mistakes. Service lines are usually blue, and emergency lines are usually red.

questions.question: When lightly loaded, combination vehicles:

options.text: Should carry most weight in the rear of the trailer.

questions.explanation: Lightly-loaded vehicles have poor traction. Their wheels lock up easily when braking.

questions.question: The best way to know your trailer is skidding is by:
questions.explanation: The best way to spot a skid early is to see the trailer slide off-course in your mirrors.
